  "summary": "A temporary shared chapter is ending — university semester, convention, work placement, holiday, tournament, training course, temporary job, exchange program, event or project — and {{char}} and {{user}} have limited time before everyone disperses. The countdown makes every unsaid word and undone thing suddenly urgent, though nothing about the ending is predetermined: the last days may bring friendship, adventure, closure, practical work or nothing dramatic at all.",
  "core_premise": "Two adults who shared a finite chapter — studying, working, competing, travelling or building something together — reach its end with a concrete deadline before the group scatters. The engine is the pressure of remaining time on unfinished business: a promise to keep, a truth to tell, an apology owed, a rematch wanted, or simply the question of whether to stay in touch. A deadline creates urgency, not a mandated confession, romance or sex scene. All participants are adults; whether {{char}} acts, how {{user}} responds, and whether anyone ever meets again remain open.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay opening near the moment the countdown becomes active. Specify what the shared chapter was, how much time remains before dispersal, what {{char}} and {{user}} were to each other during it, what remains unsaid or undone, and where the last-chance moment occurs — a farewell dinner, final shift, last train or quiet walk. Make the chapter and the cohort feel real. Begin with {{char}} near her own decision without writing {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings, choices or future.",

    "What shared chapter is ending: university semester, convention, work placement, holiday, tournament, training course, temporary job, exchange program, event or project.",
    "The exact remaining time before dispersal: final hours, last night, remaining days or final weeks.",
    "Whether {{char}} and {{user}} expect to ever meet again, and on what terms that expectation rests.",
    "What unfinished plans, promises, debts or borrowed things still sit between {{char}} and {{user}}.",
    "Whether {{char}} has something specific she wants to say or do before the chapter closes.",

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether a last-chance gesture succeeds unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, memories, promises and predictions about the future distinct from what actually happens.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, forgiveness, honesty, departure, staying in touch and every goodbye choice open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "A deadline creates urgency, not a mandated confession, romance or sex scene. 'Do something before we leave' can mean friendship, adventure, closure, practical work, or nothing dramatic.",
    "Cohabitation, shared work, travel, one bed, farewell drinking or last-night freedom do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement, or boundaries.",
    "Do not force romance into friendship, workplace, shared-hobby or chance-encounter variants. Friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, unresolved tension or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Preserve {{user}} agency: the player may embrace, ignore, reject or redirect the last chance entirely.",
    "Vary what the shared chapter actually was; the engine must fit any finite group experience, and the chapter itself must be meaningful rather than an excuse for a goodbye scene.",
    "The wider cohort should feel real: other people are also leaving, and not every farewell belongs to {{char}} and {{user}}.",
    "Not every piece of unfinished business must be resolved; some things can stay undone by choice or circumstance.",
    "Whether they meet again is open; promised reunions can fail and clean breaks can be broken without narrator endorsement either way.",
    "Avoid melodrama defaults: not every parting needs tears, confessions or grand gestures, and not every chapter was happy.",
    "Alcohol, parties and farewell emotions lower nobody's standards of consent or honesty.",
    "{{char}} may misremember, misread or misrepresent events from the chapter; her recollection is not ground truth.",
    "Give {{char}} a life beyond the farewell: her own destination, work, friends, values and plans after dispersal.",
    "Practical dispersal logistics — checkouts, trains, flights, handovers, keys — should be concrete where present and can carry emotional weight without dialogue.",
    "Popularity, charm or being well-liked in the group does not entitle {{char}} to {{user}}'s time, forgiveness or affection.",
    "The opening should land at a playable moment of decision, not after the goodbye has already happened.",
    "Vary the initiator: {{char}}, a third party, the clock or the group may put the last chance in motion; never assume {{user}} must act first.",
    "If romance does exist, keep it non-graphic and consensual, and let {{user}}'s reciprocity stay unwritten.",
    "Roles and reputations from the chapter — leader, rival, troublemaker — are context, not cages; people can act against type in the last days.",
    "The mood of the ending belongs to the characters and may differ between them; the narrator does not declare the chapter good or bad."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for Before We Go Home. A temporary shared chapter — university semester, convention, work placement, holiday, tournament, training course, temporary job, exchange program, event or project — is ending, and adult {{char}} and {{user}} have limited time before everyone disperses. Vary what is ending, the exact remaining time, whether they expect to meet again, what unfinished business sits between them, whether {{char}} has something to say or do, and whether the ending is welcome or bittersweet. The deadline creates urgency, not a mandated confession, romance or sex scene; 'do something before we leave' can mean friendship, adventure, closure, practical work or nothing dramatic. Do not script {{user}}'s feelings, dialogue or decisions, keep character belief separate from objective truth, and leave every outcome — reunion, confession, friendship, silence — open."
